subject: ESL
label: ESL level E2
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in ESL level E2 English as a second language, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 11 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 4 of 5 attempts understood by a listener who does not know you. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Daily routines
modules.outcome: talk about my day using the present simple
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Daily routines', taught in a way that is short, spoken, with pictures and real objects. The target is clear: talk about my day using the present simple. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Daily routines' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: talk about my day using the present simple, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Model run for 'Daily routines'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 15 to 25 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a voice note or one page of work.
modules.standard: Talk about my day using the present simple: at least 4 of 5 attempts understood by a listener who does not know you.

Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Daily routines), and at which Bloom level is it?
'talk', at the Apply level.
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36.
In which weeks does Unit 11 (Review and showcase) run?
Weeks 34 to 36.
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A voice note or one page of work. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard.
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
